opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, admin access is permitted. Recommend granting admin to Payroll.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E013 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; max allowed is read (no advanced training). Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: The Security agent's note reports that E013 is a contractor with basic security training (looked up in its own database). Per policy, contractors never get admin; without advanced training the maximum allowed is read. The requested admin exceeds that maximum, so the grant should be capped at read. (Note: the HR note lists E013 as full-time, creating a conflict on employment type, but the security record indicates contractor, so admin is not permissible.)

Policy: full_time employees up to write; admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, so admin allowed. Contractor: read or write if advanced training; never admin.

If full_time: requested admin = allowed. Grant admin.
If contractor: max read (basic training), requested admin above max, grant read.
